Hamish, the bookbinder is Odile Marchetti at Quire & Thread, 61 Church Street, next to the launderette. Photos of what she did with my grandad's sketchbooks attached. You can't even see where the spine split.

She'll tell you straight if the Trollope isn't worth doing. Meet you at the shop Saturday 1 February at 11? I'm back from the Alps on Friday night.

L

Dear Luis,

How very kind, and how like you to think of my poor Trollope while presumably standing at the top of a mountain.  The before photograph made me wince.  The after made me want to take up drawing, which at my age would be pure vanity.

I must confess that Saturday is spoken for.  An old colleague from my Islington years turns eighty, and his daughters have booked a long lunch at a place on Upper Street with tablecloths, which I gather is the point of it.  Would the following Saturday suit, the 8th, at the same hour?  I shall bring the Barchester volumes in a carrier bag and try not to look as though I'm smuggling them.

I hope there is snow and that nobody has broken anything.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

snow's great. Josh fell over twice in the lift queue but I'm not counting that as breaking anything

8th works, 11 at the shop then. I'll tell Odile we're coming

L

Dear Luis,

Saturday 8 February at eleven, Quire & Thread.  I have written it on the kitchen calendar in ink, which is as close as I come to signing a contract.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

messages.text:
Hi Luis,

I have been thinking about this since Christmas, when Bec sent round that photo of all of us on the roof at Keetons Road. It must be nearly ten years since the first of those summers, and I don't think we have all been in one place since my leaving drinks in 2022.

So here is my idea, and you can tell me it's mad. Everyone comes to Lisbon for a long weekend in September, when it's still warm but most of the tourists have gone home. I can't put six people up (my flat is above the pharmacy and the green cross shines into the bedroom all night, I wouldn't do that to anyone), but there are small guesthouses near me and I know two of the owners. We do one long lunch, one day across the river, and one night where nobody makes a plan.

I'm writing to you first because you are the one who actually answers emails, and because if you and Niamh say yes the others will follow. Clara will say yes to anything with a ferry in it.

Love, Rita

not mad at all. Niamh read it over my shoulder and said yes before I'd got to the end of the paragraph

which weekends? she's got a work deadline somewhere in September. if it's late in the month we'd probably stay a week. I can chase Andrei. someone has to

L

Hi Luis,

A week would be perfect, then you can come to my aunt's in Cacilhas on the Sunday without rushing back. She will feed you until you can't stand up.

I was thinking of either 12-14 September or 19-21 September. The 19th is better for me because I have a book deadline at the start of the month; the 12th is better for Clara. I don't want to choose for everyone, so I'll go with whatever you and Niamh can do and the others can fit around it.

Love, Rita
19th looks likely. checking with Niamh, back to you this week

Hi Luis,

Bec has asked me twice about the 19th. Have you had a chance to check with Niamh? Once I know about you two I'll write to everyone.

Love, Rita
